DATE:  APRIL 20, 2021
TO:  HONORABLE MAYOR AND CITY COUNCIL
FROM:  PUBLIC WORKS DEPARTMENT
  CAPITAL IMPROVEMENT PROGRAM DIVISION
DISTRICT:  1, 3, AND 4
SUBJECT:  APPROVE THE SECOND AMENDMENT TO AGREEMENT NO. A-
  6715, BETWEEN THE CITY OF PALMDALE AND SOUTHSTAR
  ENGINEERING & CONSULTING, INC., IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $385,975.

ISSUE
Approve the Second Amendment to Agreement No. A-6715, between the City of
Palmdale and Southstar Engineering & Consulting, Inc., in the amount of $385,975, in
association with construction management and materials testing services on the
Pearblossom Highway Reconstruction Project.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Approve the Second Amendment to Agreement No. A-6715, between the City of
  Palmdale and Southstar Engineering & Consulting, Inc.
  2. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute the Second Amendment to
  Agreement No. A-6715 with Southstar Engineering & Consulting, Inc., including
  minimal and/or non-substantive changes.

BACKGROUND
The Pearblossom Highway Reconstruction Project (City Project No. 696) provided for the
full-width reconstruction of 3.2 miles of Pearblossom Hwy, from the California Aqueduct
bridge to 55th Street East. The work included full excavation of the existing asphalt-
concrete roadway, up to 24 inches deep. The roadway was rebuilt with a 19.4-inch stack
of multiple material layers, including a synthetic geogrid, aggregate base, concrete base,
and asphalt-concrete, creating a strong structural section that provides a long-life solution
to support the high volume of cars and the heavy truck traffic on Pearblossom Hwy. Safety
improvements were constructed as well, including a half-mile long center median barrier,
a protective barrier for the Barrel Springs Elementary school property, new metal beam
guardrail, and new high-visibility striping. Work on the Pearblossom Hwy Reconstruction
Project began in September of 2019 and was implemented in three distinct segments,
each with its own work scope and traffic management plan.

  4
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Agreement No. A-6715, Amendment No. 2
April 20, 2021
Page 2

Due to the large extent of the project and the community impact, the City determined that
a construction management firm was necessary for this job. In June 2019, Southstar
Engineering & Consulting, Inc. (Southstar) was awarded the contract for construction
management services for the Pearblossom Highway Reconstruction Project (Agreement
No. A-6715). The scope of the construction management agreement included
comprehensive construction management (CM) services, including but not limited to:
administration of the construction contract; community outreach, such as production of
construction updates and notifications to residents, maintenance of the automatic
notification email list and the project website, and management of calls from the public;
responsibility for the review and approval of material submittals, requests for information
(RFIs), and contract change order (CCO) proposals; construction and traffic control
inspection; validation of schedules and monitoring work progress; and, materials testing
and quality control for construction surveys. Agreement No. A-6715 with Southstar for CM
services on the project was executed in the amount of $1,690,077, which included
$1,432,652 of CM work by Southstar, plus $199,560 for materials testing and $57,865 for
construction survey by subconsultants.

Construction on the Pearblossom Hwy Reconstruction Project was originally scheduled
for completion in mid-October of 2020. Southstar’s original Agreement No. A-6715
generally matched this timetable, but several construction issues encountered resulted in
the premature expenditure of contract hours by the end of September 2020. One
construction issue, that consumed CM hours, was the concrete failure of the intersection
approaches at 40th Street East, which required development of a new concrete mix design
and corrective work by the Contractor. This was the primary cause of the project delay,
requiring extra CM hours between June 2020 and September 2020, and then further into
December 2020 to fully resolve.

The City requested Southstar provide a proposal to continue CM services as the project
was not yet complete and ongoing CM services are necessary for the success of the
project. Southstar submitted a proposal for the actual cost of CM services and materials
testing provided at the end of September 2020 and through October 2020. The City and
Southstar mutually agreed to Amendment No. 1 in the amount of $168,800, which
included an additional 572 hours of CM services and $65,000 for materials testing. The
City then requested Southstar submit a proposal for Amendment No. 2, projecting the
cost of ongoing CM services through the end of the project, which at that point was
expected to be complete in December 2020.

In early December 2020, City staff reviewed the condition of project site in Segment 1
and identified a safety need to widen the shoulders of Pearblossom Hwy between 25th
Street East and 30th Street East. Implementing the widening was challenging due to
physical constraints, and ultimately the City decided to postpone the shoulder widening
for a future project. Planning and preparing for the shoulder widening delayed completion
of the remaining project work in Segment 1 and extended the closure, requiring the

  5
 Report to Mayor and City Council
Re: Agreement No. A-6715, Amendment No. 2
April 20, 2021
Page 3

continued presence of Southstar as CM. The remaining project work was finalized, and
Pearblossom Highway was successfully reopened to the public on February 25, 2021.

The City asked Southstar to revise their proposal to reflect the actual CM work that was
performed. Southstar submitted a revised proposal for Amendment No. 2 to Agreement
No. A-6715 that includes actual compensation costs for the provision of CM services for
November and December 2020, January and February 2021, and a projection for March
2021. The proposal for Amendment No. 2 includes 2,007 hours or $379,527.80 of CM
services and $6,447 for materials testing, representing actual costs for services provided
except for a projection of 200 hours of CM services in March. Although the roadway is
open to the public, there is remaining project closeout work to do, including a pending
construction claim that requires Southstar’s ongoing involvement in March.

DISCUSSION
Due to the delays on the project, Southstar exceeded their original agreement amount
earlier than expected, but the provision of ongoing CM services was necessary to
complete the project. The construction management service is within the typical
percentage of a CM agreement, typically 12%-18% of the construction costs. The
Southstar CM agreement history is summarized in the following table:

FISCAL IMPACT
Funds for this increase exist in the S0057 account with a current available balance of
approx. $1.2 million.
